projectDescription: A dating and local-exploration app that helps people discover nearby places and connect through shared interests and experiences.

services.name: Roamora API
services.phase: Later phases: accounts, matching, location-aware drops, and chat

questions.question: Which language should the Roamora frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Recommended for a maintainable frontend with safer API contracts.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: A lighter setup without static type checking.

questions.rationale: A typed frontend is a good default for an app that will grow from a frontend-first MVP into API-backed features.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should Roamora use?
questions.recommendedChoice: Next.js with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS

options.label: React
options.description: Recommended ecosystem for a responsive, component-based web app.

options.label: Vue
options.description: A progressive framework with a approachable component model.

options.label: Svelte
options.description: A compiler-based framework for concise interactive interfaces.

options.label: Angular
options.description: A comprehensive framework with an opinionated application structure.

options.label: Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript
options.description: A minimal option for a small static experience.

questions.answer: Next.js with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS
questions.rationale: Next.js with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS matches the requested frontend stack and supports an interactive, responsive app.

questions.question: What should the frontend-first MVP include?
questions.recommendedChoice: Responsive discovery experience with onboarding, editable profile, interest-based nearby exploration, map/list views, and clearly labeled sample data; defer live GPS, matching, and chat until later phases.
questions.answer: Responsive discovery experience with onboarding, editable profile, interest-based nearby exploration, map/list views, and clearly labeled sample data; defer live GPS, matching, and chat until later phases.
questions.rationale: This delivers a coherent frontend-first product while keeping sensitive location and social interactions out of the initial mock-data phase.

questions.question: Which language should the later Roamora API use?

options.label: C#
options.description: Recommended for a Node.js and Express API.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Use a shared language across frontend and API.

options.label: Java
options.description: Use a mature JVM backend ecosystem.

options.label: Python
options.description: Use a concise backend language with a broad ecosystem.

questions.rationale: TypeScript keeps the API aligned with the requested Node.js and Express backend.

questions.question: Which backend framework should Roamora use in a later phase?

options.label: Express.js
options.description: Recommended Node.js framework for Roamora's REST API.

options.label: ASP.NET Core Web API
options.description: A controller-based structure for a larger API.

options.label: Express.js
options.description: A minimal Node.js framework, typically paired with TypeScript.

options.label: FastAPI
options.description: A Python API framework with typed request/response support.

questions.rationale: Express.js provides the requested REST API framework and can grow incrementally with the Roamora features.

questions.question: What should the later API phase cover?
questions.recommendedChoice: Add account/profile APIs first, then persisted exploration drops and opt-in GPS discovery, followed by mutual-interest matching and private chat; enforce consent, location privacy, blocking, and reporting.
questions.answer: Add account/profile APIs first, then persisted exploration drops and opt-in GPS discovery, followed by mutual-interest matching and private chat; enforce consent, location privacy, blocking, and reporting.
questions.rationale: The staged sequence keeps the first release frontend-focused and introduces sensitive social/location capabilities only with backend controls.

questions.question: Which data stores will the planned app need?

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Relational storage for accounts, profiles, preferences, exploration drops, matches, and chat metadata.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Object storage for profile photos and other user-uploaded media.

options.label: Azure SQL
options.description: Managed relational database alternative.

options.label: Cosmos DB
options.description: Globally distributed NoSQL database option.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use only if the app will not persist data, files, queues, or cache.

questions.rationale: The later account, discovery, matching, and chat features require persistence; dating profiles commonly include user photos.

questions.question: Will users sign in to use Roamora's application features?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users have accounts for profiles and future matching or chat.

options.label: No
options.description: The app remains anonymous and does not provide account-backed features.

questions.rationale: Accounts are necessary for the planned dating profiles, saved preferences, matches, and private conversations; authentication can be deferred from the frontend-first phase.
